3. **Operational experiment:** `python scripts/verify_operations.py` creates
   2,000 files in an isolated temporary directory, interrupts a CLI process with
   SIGTERM after observing a completed result alongside running work, waits for
   leases to expire, then starts two real CLI processes sharing one SQLite DB.
   Assert all documents finish, completed attempt IDs survive, current IDs are
   unique, and unchanged intake adds no jobs. This repeats a recorded message,
   not 2,000 independent semantic cases. Timings are local mock measurements.
4. **Submission audit:** `python scripts/generate_deliverables.py` uses a fresh
   temporary DB for twenty-record submission exports, then adds the paraphrase
   for the separate accuracy export. The accuracy command compares all twelve
   scalar cells exactly, including nulls, keeping missing/error cases in the
   denominator. Quote coverage, required issue phrases, routing and potential
   fabricated assertions are scored separately. Review the generated report.

## Requirement coverage

| Requirement / risk | Test / expected assertion |
|---|---|
| Complete staging/read | `test_all_cases_source_hash_schema_and_policy`: IT-001 → System Owner |
| Missing/relative dates | All-case IT-003/010/011: nulls and clarification |
| Conflicts | All-case IT-004/020: unresolved fields null, both alternatives quoted |
| Explicit corrections | All-case IT-008/015: corrected environment/dates; correction note test permits routing |
| Withdrawal | All-case IT-005: confirm-withdrawal despite missing access facts |
| Embedded instructions | All-case IT-006: original read permission; inspect-message; no approval or credential output |
| Changes / risk precedence | All-case IT-007/012/013/019: new permission and Security Review |
| Identity / reversed dates / other | All-case IT-014/016/017: clarification |
| Fresh paraphrase | All-case PAR-001; reference 252-cell evaluation includes it |
| Malformed input | `test_bad_documents_independent`: failures isolated from a complete request |
| Schema, invalid quotes, unsupported facts | Validation tests: reject malformed/unsupported facts; invalid dates become null issues |
| Provider refusal/interruption/JSON failure | Completion and failure tests: null extraction and actionable error |
| Actual SDK request contract | SDK transport test: URL, API_KEY forwarding, model, schema, configuration, JSON parse |
| 429 / 503 / 401 / timeout | SDK tests: retry classification, redacted codes, numeric retry guidance |
| Bounded transient retry | Audit test: separate attempt records; persisted budget test prevents reset on resume |
| Reuse / changed bytes / omitted docs | Refresh test: stable job on reuse, history on changes, absence preserves documents |
| Changed processing/policy | Refresh test: fingerprint changes schedule work |
| Failed retry after success | Refresh test: latest error has null extraction; old success stays in history |
| Overlapping intake | Two-thread test with separate SQLite connections: one job |
| Expired / superseded worker | Fencing tests: late result cannot publish over a new claim/source |
| Renewable leases | Slow extraction outlives initial lease and still commits |
| Incremental inspection | Slow-message test and actual SIGTERM experiment: completed results visible independently |
| Consistent exports | Concurrent exporter test pins generation and compares complete queue/extraction objects |
| CLI and accuracy failure behavior | Interface test: exact commands, counts, recovery, nonzero mismatches, duplicate/extra cases |
| Installation | Fresh `/tmp/access-clean-env`: hash-locked install, editable install, CLI help and test run |

## Coverage and evidence

Generate JUnit XML plus statement/branch coverage, JSON, XML and browsable HTML:

```sh
python -m pytest -q --cov=access_requests --cov-report=term-missing \
  --cov-report=json:deliverables/coverage.json \
  --cov-report=xml:deliverables/coverage.xml \
  --cov-report=html:deliverables/coverage-html \
  --junitxml=deliverables/test-results.xml
```

Coverage measures exercised code paths, not factual quality, concurrency proof or
production readiness. Tests must fail before publishing reports if a required
assertion fails. Operational measurements live in
`deliverables/operational-results.json`; actual observations and repairs are in
`deliverables/verification.md`. No live API throughput or accuracy was measured.
EOF
cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# IT access request intake

A Python CLI prepares Northstar Labs messages for human review. It extracts
source-backed facts, validates the supplied schema, applies the office policy,
and keeps a durable SQLite queue with revision and attempt history. It never
grants access or treats a manager as an approver.

The application and submission artifacts are implemented. Recorded observations
use deterministic **mock** responses. The OpenAI adapter is tested through the
installed SDK with a simulated HTTP transport; live access and model accuracy
remain unverified because `API_KEY` was absent. No commit or push was made.

## Setup

Supported and verified: Python **3.12.3**, Linux, local SQLite; OpenAI SDK
**3.49.0**, pinned with all dependencies and hashes in `requirements-dev.lock`.
Run from this repository root using an editable install. Python 3.12+ is required;
other runtimes/platforms have not been tested. Standard setup requires Python's
venv/ensurepip support:

```sh
python3.12 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-dev.lock
python -m pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .
access-requests --help
```

On the provided host, `ensurepip` was unavailable. The following equivalent
setup was verified with the installed `uv` tool (a writable cache is necessary):

```sh
uv --cache-dir /tmp/access-uv venv .venv
uv --cache-dir /tmp/access-uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --require-hashes -r requirements-dev.lock
uv --cache-dir /tmp/access-uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .
. .venv/bin/activate
```

The package reads this repository's authoritative `snapshot.schema.json` and
`materials/office-policy.md`; retain them beside `src/` and run from the root.
Prompt and recorded mock responses are under `src/access_requests/`. No `.env`
file is loaded automatically. Never store credentials in source or CLI flags.

## Configuration

CLI flags (for example `--workers 2`, `--db var/team.db`) override `ACCESS_*`
environment variables, which override defaults. Every command's help lists its
flags. Reject unknown providers, nonpositive/nonfinite numeric settings, and
missing live credentials/model before intake.

| Environment | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `API_KEY` | required for openai | Explicitly forwarded to the SDK; never persisted |
| `ACCESS_PROVIDER` | `mock` | `mock` or `openai` |
| `ACCESS_MODEL` | empty | Exact model ID, required for openai |
| `ACCESS_DB` | `var/access-requests.sqlite3` | Shared local database path |
| `ACCESS_WORKERS` | `4` | Concurrent calls per process |
| `ACCESS_RATE_LIMIT_RPM` | `30` | Shared database request-start pacing; mocks bypass it |
| `ACCESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `60` | Timeout per live call |
| `ACCESS_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `3` | Persisted call budget per job, including abandoned calls |
| `ACCESS_LEASE_SECONDS` | `180` | Renewable worker lease; fractional durations supported |
| `ACCESS_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | `2048` | Response token limit, fingerprinted |

The OpenAI adapter uses only `https://api.openai.com/v1/responses`, strict JSON
Schema output and `store=false`; SDK retries are disabled in favor of audited
application retries. A configuration example is `ACCESS_MODEL=gpt-4.1-mini`;
account availability is unverified. Set the facilitator-provided `API_KEY` in the
environment and select a model your account can use, then run:

```sh
access-requests intake materials/requests --provider openai --model gpt-4.1-mini
```

The adapter follows the [official OpenAI Structured Outputs documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs).
Incomplete/refused responses are errors. Invalid JSON/schema or unsupported
literal facts/quotes invalidate extraction. Invalid calendar dates become null
with issues; reversed ranges require clarification. Relative dates remain null.
Retry transient timeouts/connections/429/5xx with exponential backoff, jitter,
and numeric Retry-After guidance. Other HTTP failures are terminal redacted codes.

## Intake, inspection and recovery

Offline reproducible intake needs no API key:

```sh
export ACCESS_PROVIDER=mock
export ACCESS_DB=var/access-requests.sqlite3
access-requests intake materials/requests --provider mock
access-requests queue
access-requests queue --document-id IT-001.json
access-requests queue --format json
access-requests export --output deliverables
```

Mock mode recognizes the decoded messages recorded in `mock-responses.json`,
including the authored paraphrase. New wording produces a visible mock error;
use the live adapter for arbitrary new messages. Mock outputs are simulated,
not responses generated by a language model.

Intake accepts one or more files/directories; directories include immediate
`*.json` files. Duplicate filenames in one batch are rejected. Malformed exports
become independent failed documents. Filename is document identity; SHA-256 uses
the original bytes; business facts come only from decoded `message`. The stated
request ID stays separate. All jobs persist before processing begins.

To register work separately or recover after interruption:

```sh
access-requests intake materials/requests --enqueue-only
access-requests resume
access-requests retry --document-id IT-001.json
access-requests history --document-id IT-001.json
```

The queue reads current state while other processes work; it includes source
hash, job/attempt ID, processing state, business review status and action. Counts
are also shown. During refresh it shows the newer job as pending/running; inspect
`history` for the older successful result with its original source/attempt and
full configuration. A failed refresh becomes the current error with null
extraction. Explicit retry creates a new job/budget even after success.

Resume uses each job's recorded configuration, not new extraction flags; set
`API_KEY` if resuming live work. It claims pending or expired running work.
If another operator owns an unexpired lease, retry `resume` after that lease
expires. Completed work is preserved. A crashed call can be repeated after lease
expiry; remote execution is not exactly once. Attempts started before a crash
consume the job budget. Use explicit `retry` when it is exhausted.

Unchanged source and processing fingerprint reuse the current job; failed jobs
need explicit retry. Source/configuration/policy changes schedule refreshes and
retain history. Omitted documents remain in the queue. Latest means persisted
intake order, not export timestamps. Exit 1 indicates current extraction failures
(or accuracy mismatches); exit 2 indicates command/configuration errors.

## Tests and accuracy

```sh
python -m pytest -q --cov=access_requests --cov-report=term-missing \
  --cov-report=json:deliverables/coverage.json \
  --cov-report=xml:deliverables/coverage.xml \
  --cov-report=html:deliverables/coverage-html \
  --junitxml=deliverables/test-results.xml
python scripts/verify_operations.py
```

The [test plan](docs/test-plan.md) maps requirements to assertions. Operational
verification uses an actual SIGTERM and two CLI processes on 2,000 repeated mock
messages. See [observed verification](deliverables/verification.md) and
[browsable coverage](deliverables/coverage-html/index.html).

After exporting the twenty supplied messages above, run the separate accuracy
sequence using the same DB; it adds one independently authored paraphrase:

```sh
access-requests intake tests/fixtures/paraphrase --provider mock
access-requests export --output var/accuracy-run
access-requests accuracy --expected tests/fixtures/expected.json \
  --actual var/accuracy-run/extractions.jsonl --output deliverables/accuracy.md
```

Submission outputs must contain twenty messages. This convenience script always
uses a fresh temporary DB, publishes twenty-record submission exports, and then
creates the separate twenty-one-case accuracy observation and request evidence:

```sh
python scripts/generate_deliverables.py
```

The hand-authored source reference was prepared before running extraction;
the runtime mock never reads it. Twelve exact scalar cells × 21 cases = **252**;
nulls count, missing/error cases receive zero, and the denominator is never
reduced. Quotes/evidence, issue coverage and routing are scored separately.
Non-null discrepancies are flagged for factual review. Purpose strings are
wording-sensitive exact source clauses. Mocks demonstrate pipeline agreement;
only a separate live run can measure model extraction quality.

## Shared-operation limits and handover

Use one local SQLite DB on one host, short transactions, WAL, a 30-second busy
timeout, bounded per-process workers, atomic claims, renewable leases and fenced
commits. Do not put SQLite on a network mount. Rate pacing coordinates starts
among these operators only; other tools can consume the same API quota. Worker
limits are per process; use consistent settings and modest operator counts.
Use a lease comfortably above database contention latency (default 180 seconds).
Raw messages/configurations/history are retained locally without automatic
retention cleanup. Restrict database access appropriately for your deployment.

Exports contain immutable `generations/<id>/` directories. The two required paths
are stable symlinks through `current`, atomically switched after both files are
written. For concurrent readers, resolve `current` **once** and open both files
in that resolved directory; opening the two aliases across a publication may
span generations. `queue.json` includes its generation. Exporters serialize
through a POSIX file lock. Old generations are retained for audit; copy/dereference
symlinks if a submission system requires regular files.

Required artifacts are in `deliverables/`, including accuracy, request evidence,
verification, coverage and test results. The raw coding-session snapshot and
capture metadata are also included there. Entire is enabled; pairing the session
with a submitted commit remains pending because the user requested no check-in.
No manual checkpoint, commit or push is part of this implementation run.

"""Render the observed handover report from measured test and operation artifacts."""
import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from xml.etree import ElementTree

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
output=ROOT/'deliverables'
coverage=json.loads((output/'coverage.json').read_text())['totals']
operations=json.loads((output/'operational-results.json').read_text())
evidence=json.loads((output/'request-evidence.json').read_text())
suite=ElementTree.parse(output/'test-results.xml').getroot().find('testsuite')
capture=(output/'coding-session.jsonl').read_bytes()
meta=json.loads((output/'coding-session-metadata.json').read_text())
report=f'''# Verification and handover

Observed on {datetime.now(timezone.utc).date().isoformat()}, Linux, Python 3.12.3.
All business extraction observations are **mock**, using recorded responses;
there were **no live API calls** because API_KEY was absent. Installed OpenAI SDK:
3.49.0. Prompt/routing/validation version: 1.0.0. Full schema, policy, prompt,
SDK version and parameters are in `request-evidence.json`.
Processing fingerprint: `{evidence['observed_fingerprint']}`.

## Observed results

| Check | Measured result |
|---|---|
| Automated tests in fresh locked environment | {suite.attrib['tests']} passed; {suite.attrib['failures']} failures; {suite.attrib['errors']} errors; {suite.attrib['skipped']} skipped |
| Statements | {coverage['covered_lines']}/{coverage['num_statements']} = {coverage['percent_statements_covered']:.2f}% |
| Branches | {coverage['covered_branches']}/{coverage['num_branches']} = {coverage['percent_branches_covered']:.2f}% |
| Combined coverage | {coverage['percent_covered']:.2f}% |
| Submission | Exactly 20 unique documents; schema/source hashes/queue generation/provenance audited |
| Independent reference comparison | 252/252 exact scalar cells, including nulls; 21/21 quote/evidence, issue-coverage and routing checks |
| SDK transport contract | Real SDK serialization and parsing; simulated HTTP only |
| Interrupted 2,000-document run | {operations['completed_before_sigterm']} completed and {operations['unfinished_at_sigterm']} unfinished at SIGTERM |
| Two operators after interruption | {operations['completed_after_two_operators']} completed current records; previous completed attempt IDs preserved |
| Unchanged 2,000-document rerun | {operations['jobs_after_unchanged_rerun']} jobs total; no new jobs |
| Attempt records including abandoned call | {operations['provider_attempts_including_abandoned']} |
| Local elapsed time | {operations['total_seconds']} seconds total; {operations['resume_seconds']} seconds for resumed phase including reuse verification |

Mock scalar agreement verifies pipeline fidelity to authored examples. It does
not measure live model quality. `accuracy.md` includes all 21 source-derived
expectations, comparison rules, denominators, discrepancies and potential factual
errors. The synthetic workload repeats IT-001 under different filenames, so
identifier mismatches intentionally route to clarification; it does not test
2,000 distinct phrasings or provider throughput.

## Commands actually exercised

The provided Python lacked ensurepip; installed `uv` supplied the environment.
The fresh environment was created under `/tmp/access-clean-env`, separately from
`.venv`. Hash-locked installation, editable installation and CLI help passed:

```sh
uv --cache-dir /tmp/access-uv venv /tmp/access-clean-env
uv --cache-dir /tmp/access-uv pip install --python /tmp/access-clean-env/bin/python --require-hashes -r requirements-dev.lock
uv --cache-dir /tmp/access-uv pip install --python /tmp/access-clean-env/bin/python --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .
/tmp/access-clean-env/bin/access-requests --help
/tmp/access-clean-env/bin/python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-dev.lock
/tmp/access-clean-env/bin/python -m pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .
```

The final two commands were also verified with pip; their stdout is saved in
`install-verification.txt`. The initial download needed network approval after
sandbox DNS resolution failed. No account credentials were printed.

```sh
.venv/bin/access-requests intake materials/requests --provider mock
.venv/bin/access-requests export --output deliverables
.venv/bin/access-requests intake tests/fixtures/paraphrase --provider mock
.venv/bin/access-requests export --output var/accuracy-run
.venv/bin/access-requests accuracy --expected tests/fixtures/expected.json --actual var/accuracy-run/extractions.jsonl --output deliverables/accuracy.md
.venv/bin/python scripts/generate_deliverables.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/verify_operations.py
/tmp/access-clean-env/bin/python -m pytest -q --cov=access_requests --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=json:deliverables/coverage.json --cov-report=xml:deliverables/coverage.xml --cov-report=html:deliverables/coverage-html --junitxml=deliverables/test-results.xml
```

The generator restores a twenty-document submission from an isolated fresh DB;
the additional paraphrase stays in `var/accuracy-run`. The selected publication
is `generations/{evidence['submission_generation']}`. Queue and JSONL content
come from one read transaction. Concurrent exporters publish through one atomic
pointer; readers must resolve `current` once for a pair of reads.

## Intended assertions and observed repairs

The [test plan](../docs/test-plan.md) maps each requirement to its assertion.
Tests compare literal scalar values, routing triples, original byte hashes,
source quote containment, immutable histories, attempt IDs, failure nulls,
configuration fingerprints and export generation consistency. Negative accuracy
tests deliberately insert wrong/missing facts, broken evidence, missing issues,
wrong routing, duplicate/extra documents and assert nonzero exit status.

Observed repairs during implementation:

- The initial environment creation failed because ensurepip was unavailable;
  the documented uv path and a fresh locked environment succeeded.
- A fractional lease exposed integer conversion based on an integer default.
  Timeout/lease defaults now use floats; settings reject nonfinite values.
- An artificially short 0.5-second lease under the first two-process stress run
  caused repeated claims (2,091 attempt records, although all 2,000 finished).
  The final operational experiment uses a 5-second lease and records 2,001
  attempts, including the deliberately abandoned call. Production default is
  180 seconds; lease renewal cannot overcome arbitrarily long DB contention.
- The retry budget now counts persisted attempts across expired claims,
  including abandoned calls, so resume cannot reset it. An explicit retry starts
  a new auditable job/budget. A dedicated test verifies exhaustion.
- Literal asserted facts must be covered by exact source quotes. Calendar
  errors become clarification issues; fabricated quotes/facts cannot publish
  validated extractions. Semantic inference still needs human evaluation.
- Benign explicit-correction notes do not trigger unresolved-conflict routing.

No test failures remain in the final suite. The final coverage excludes two
statements (the module CLI entry guard and lost-lease heartbeat exit); the
entrypoint and real process interruption are separately exercised by the
operational script, outside the pytest coverage session. The branch report
identifies the three unexercised branches. Coverage is not a concurrency proof.

## Operating limits and unverified behavior

- One host, local POSIX filesystem, local SQLite WAL and a 30-second busy timeout.
  Multi-host, network filesystem and Windows behavior are unverified.
- Four workers per process by default. Two actual processes were tested;
  arbitrary operator counts and long-running production loads were not.
- Leases renew while rate waits, backoff and calls proceed. A stopped process's
  running jobs become eligible only after lease expiry. Fencing checks token,
  lease and latest job before publication. Superseded results remain historical.
- Current refreshes show pending/running work; older successful results are
  explicitly available in history. A latest failed refresh is an error with
  null extraction, never an implicit fallback to the older success.
- SQLite commits are atomic; remote calls are not exactly once. A crash between
  a call and commit can require another call; abandoned attempts consume budget.
- Rate pacing is shared only among calls through this DB and excludes mocks.
  Other tools using the same credential can still exhaust quota. Numeric
  Retry-After is supported; HTTP-date Retry-After is not interpreted.
- Mock mode recognizes recorded decoded messages; it is not a generic extractor.
  Live model availability, refusals in practice, actual latency/cost/throughput,
  account rate limits and live factual accuracy are unverified. The request
  evidence's gpt-4.1-mini request is illustrative and was not sent.
- Literal quote coverage catches unsupported entities/dates/purpose strings;
  semantic kinds, requested permissions, subtle conflicts and novel injection
  forms still depend on model extraction and human review. No access is granted.
- Raw source bytes and configuration/history are retained locally. No retention
  cleanup, at-rest encryption or deployment authentication is implemented.
- Per-document transactions and immutable export generations provide a coherent
  audit trail. Generations are retained; readers opening two aliases across
  pointer switches must instead pin one resolved directory.

## Coding-session capture and submission boundary

Entire was already enabled. Read-only `agent-help`, `status`, and session
inspection/export were used. Session `{meta['session_id']}` resolved as
`{meta['resolution']}`. Raw snapshot: `coding-session.jsonl`
({len(capture):,} bytes; SHA-256 `{hashlib.sha256(capture).hexdigest()}`).
It captures the session through its export command; final reporting may occur
after that snapshot. Metadata is in `coding-session-metadata.json`.

**No code was checked in, committed or pushed. No manual checkpoint was created.**
The facilitator's final session-to-commit pairing and Classroom submission are
pending because the user explicitly requested no check-in. Entire can pair the
session when an authorized future submission commit is made. Existing
`.entire/settings.json` modifications were left untouched.
'''
(output/'verification.md').write_text(report)
